newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma seizes large hauls of heroin, opium in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Burma seizes large hauls of heroin, opium in 1996.

text.p: The Burmese government said on Wednesday it seized 504 kgs (1,110 lbs) of heroin, 1.3 tonnes of opium and 263.8 kgs (582 lbs) of marijuana in its anti-narcotics campaign last year.
Burma's Central Committee for Drugs Abuse Control said some 5,540 people, including 1,013 women, were arrested on drug charges in 1996.
It said seven of the suspects were sentenced to death but government sources said some of their sentences were later commuted to long jail terms.
Burmese courts have sentenced 20 drug suspects to death and 48 have been given life jail terms since the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) took power in September 1988.
The Burmese government will torch the seized drugs in a ceremony witnessed by diplomats, United Nations officials and journalists on Thursday.

Burma is the world's largest producer of illegal opium and its refined form, heroin. The United States says about 60 percent of the heroin sold in the United States comes from Southeast Asia, with most of it coming from Burma.

The Golden Triangle, where Laos, Thailand and Burma meet, is one of the world's top heroin producing areas. The U.S. Drug Enforcement Admninistration estimates about 70 percent of heroin supplied to the international market comes from the region.
